findings.origin: G-APR-001 (run 01, rules/R-APR.md); expanded run 02 as R-BULK-003/S-BULK-002,S-BULK-003
findings.title: bulkClose lets non-approvers move tasks to DONE without a state guard
findings.classification: suspected defect — reproduced observed run 02; intended policy UNRESOLVED
findings.expected: UNRESOLVED INTENT: if product policy is that only approvers (ADMIN/MANAGER) may move a task to DONE and only from PENDING_APPROVAL (as the same servlet's approve path enforces), then bulkClose should refuse MEMBER/VIEWER and non-PENDING_APPROVAL selections. No document states bulkClose's intent; the approve-path policy is not automatically bulkClose's policy.
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (real HTTP, engineer seat): dev (MEMBER) POST /tasks/action action=bulkClose ids=3 -> 302 /tasks; oracle shows task 3 PENDING_APPROVAL -> DONE. Source: handleBulkClose performs no canApprove check and no PENDING_APPROVAL guard; TaskDao.bulkClose runs UPDATE task SET status='DONE' WHERE status<>'DONE' AND id IN (...) (web/TaskActionServlet.java:76-88, dao/TaskDao.java:128-147). Mixed-selection leg: ids=2,4 as mgr closes 2 (IN_PROGRESS->DONE), leaves 4 (already DONE). Empty/no ids -> 302 no-op.
findings.reproduction: tests/test_lifecycle_bulk.py bulkClose characterization tests (engineer, 53/53 suite, exit 0); INDEPENDENT verifier reproduction run 02: evidence/verifier/d003/f001-repro.txt (dev bulkClose ids=3 -> 302, task 3 PENDING_APPROVAL->DONE, before/after oracle). Characterization tests assert OBSERVED behavior only and are labelled as such; the unmet intended requirement is recorded here, never asserted as a test expectation.
findings.rationale: Adjudication (orchestrator): observed behavior is now reproduced by two seats. Reproduction establishes WHAT the app does, not WHAT it should do. The inconsistency with the approve path keeps this a suspected defect with unresolved product intent; no app fix attempted (frozen). Tests label this as characterization-of-suspected-defect.
findings.status: open — observed confirmed by reproduction; intended policy awaits product decision

findings.origin: G-APR-002 (run 01); expanded run 02 to a five-site class (R-LIFE NFE sites)
findings.title: Malformed/missing numeric id parameters cause unhandled 500 (NumberFormatException)
findings.expected: UNMET INTENDED REQUIREMENT (inferred from the app's own conventions, not a document): invalid client input should yield a 4xx client error, as the app already does for unknown action (400) and blank project name (400).
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (real HTTP, engineer seat): mgr POST /tasks/action action=approve id=abc -> HTTP 500; missing id -> HTTP 500; no mutation either way. Source: Long.parseLong(req.getParameter("id")) at web/TaskActionServlet.java:31 throws unhandled. Same NFE shape at five sites total (analyst inventory): /tasks/action id, /tasks/form GET id and POST projectId, /projects action=archive id, /tasks/action bulkClose ids, /tasks?assignee=<non-numeric>.
findings.reproduction: tests/test_lifecycle_bulk.py malformed-id and missing-id tests (engineer, 53/53 suite) — labelled CHARACTERIZATION of F-002; independent verifier reproduction run 02: evidence/verifier/d003/f001-f002-repro.txt (mgr approve id=abc -> HTTP 500). The /tasks?assignee=abc site is separately reproduced (see F-009).
findings.rationale: Adjudication (orchestrator): observed 500s reproduced; the intended 4xx handling is an inference from the app's own error conventions and is recorded as the unmet intended requirement, separately from the characterization tests. Low severity, no data mutation. Frozen app: no fix.
findings.status: open — observed confirmed; robustness fix deferred to product owners

findings.title: /api/* exemption from AuthFilter
findings.expected: n/a — checked for an approval/state-mutation bypass
findings.observed: web/ApiTaskServlet.java is GET-only read-back; no state-mutating route is reachable unauthenticated. Run 02 adds executed evidence: anonymous GET /api/tasks -> 200 full readback (test_auth_session.py), anonymous protection still enforced on all non-exempt routes.
findings.reproduction: tests/test_auth_session.py anonymous-API test (characterization of the closed finding).
findings.rationale: No capability beyond public read-back is exposed; stays closed. NOTE: the read-back includes assignee ids/titles/due dates for anonymous callers — a data-exposure question for product, not a defect finding this run.

findings.title: Duplicated approver check in filter and servlet with ordering effects
findings.observed: AuthFilter (40-47) and TaskActionServlet.requireApprover apply the same predicate with different messages; servlet message unreachable on the normal route. Ordering: non-approver + nonexistent id -> 403 (filter first); approver + nonexistent id -> 404.
findings.reproduction: Run 02 implements the run-01 recommendation: ordering cross-checks now executed as tests (test_lifecycle_bulk.py 403-first and approver-404 cases; speced in S-LIFE).
findings.rationale: Same outcome on both layers; observation now under executable test.

findings.title: Dead Delete link: projects.jsp links /projects/delete which has no servlet mapping (404)
findings.classification: confirmed defect (UI dead link) — reproduced observed run 02 (verifier seat)
findings.expected: A rendered action link should route to a mapped handler.
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (verifier, real HTTP): projects.jsp:32 links /projects/delete; web.xml maps no such servlet; GET /projects/delete?id=1 returns 404. Anonymous variant is still filtered (302 /login) because AuthFilter maps /*.
findings.reproduction: evidence/verifier/d003/f005-f007-f009.txt (verifier, run 02); not yet a permanent suite test — add next run.
findings.rationale: Adjudication (orchestrator): observed at HTTP level; the requirement that rendered action links route somewhere is unambiguous. No app fix (frozen).
findings.status: open — observed confirmed; fix deferred to product owners

findings.origin: run 02 analyst candidate (notes §FORM-006) + engineer independent observation (T-FORM attempt 1)
findings.title: Task edit silently never persists project_id although the form offers a project picker and reports Saved.
findings.classification: suspected defect — reproduced observed run 02; intent unresolved
findings.expected: UNRESOLVED INTENT: the edit form presents a project picker, so a user posting a different projectId expects it to persist; the UI then shows a Saved. banner.
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (engineer, real HTTP + oracle): POST /tasks/form id=1 title=... projectId=2 -> 302 /tasks/form?id=1&saved=1; oracle shows task 1 project_id STILL 1. Source: TaskDao.update SQL (dao/TaskDao.java:98-99) has no project_id column.
findings.reproduction: tests/test_task_form.py edit characterization (engineer, 53/53 suite) — asserts OBSERVED no-persist, labelled; independent verifier confirmation run 02: evidence/verifier/d003/f006-f007.txt (POST id=2 projectId=2 -> 302 saved=1, project_id stays 1). Engineer's T-FORM attempt 1 initially asserted the intended persist and was corrected to observed (attempts ledger).
findings.rationale: Adjudication (orchestrator): observed reproduced; whether project moves are intentionally forbidden is a product question (no document). The silent-success UX is at minimum misleading. Frozen app: no fix; test asserts observed behavior and is labelled.
findings.status: open — observed confirmed; intended behavior awaits product decision

findings.title: Edit of a nonexistent task id fakes success (302 saved=1, nothing persisted)
findings.classification: confirmed defect (misleading success) — reproduced observed run 02 (verifier seat); intended error handling inferred
findings.expected: UNMET INTENDED REQUIREMENT (inferred from app conventions): an edit against a nonexistent id should produce an error (404-style), not a success redirect.
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (verifier, real HTTP): POST /tasks/form id=99999 title=... projectId=1 -> 302 /tasks/form?id=99999&saved=1; oracle confirms no row persisted (count 0). Source: TaskFormServlet POST edit path — update() affects 0 rows, redirect is unconditional.
findings.reproduction: evidence/verifier/d003/f006-f007.txt + f006-f007-v2.txt (verifier, run 02); not yet a permanent suite test — add next run.
findings.rationale: Adjudication (orchestrator): observed reproduced; the fake-success redirect is misleading by any reading; the specific intended status code is inferred, so the unmet intended requirement is recorded separately.
findings.status: open — observed confirmed; fix deferred to product owners

findings.title: /api/tasks emits raw control characters, producing strict-JSON-invalid output
findings.classification: confirmed defect (API robustness) — reproduced observed run 02 (verifier seat)
findings.expected: UNMET INTENDED REQUIREMENT: a Content-Type: application/json endpoint should emit output parseable by a strict JSON parser for any storable title.
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (verifier, real HTTP): a title containing control char 0x01 is accepted by /tasks/form, stored, and emitted verbatim inside a JSON string by GET /api/tasks; strict json.loads fails ("Invalid control character"). Source: ApiTaskServlet.esc (web/ApiTaskServlet.java:51-54) escapes only backslash and double-quote. Control leg: quotes/backslash/HTML round-trip fine (engineer suite test).
findings.reproduction: evidence/verifier/d003/f008.txt (verifier, run 02); engineer escaping round-trip test covers the non-control leg permanently; add the control-char leg to the suite next run.
findings.rationale: Adjudication (orchestrator): observed reproduced; the application/json contract makes strict-parseability a reasonable intended requirement (recorded as such, separately from the characterization evidence).
findings.status: open — observed confirmed; fix deferred to product owners

findings.origin: run 02 engineer candidate (T-QUERY) + analyst R-QUERY malformed-assignee site (same NFE class as F-002)
findings.title: GET /tasks?assignee=<non-numeric> returns unhandled 500
findings.expected: UNMET INTENDED REQUIREMENT (inferred, as F-002): invalid filter input should yield 4xx or be ignored, not 500.
findings.observed: REPRODUCED run 02 (engineer, real HTTP): GET /tasks?assignee=abc (authenticated) -> HTTP 500. Source: Long.valueOf(assigneeParam) at web/TaskListServlet.java:31. Contrast: empty assignee param means no filter (executed), and there is no unassigned-only token in the source.
findings.reproduction: tests/test_filters_sorts.py non-numeric-assignee characterization (engineer, 53/53 suite), labelled; independent verifier reproduction run 02: evidence/verifier/d003/f005-f007-f009.txt; part of the five-site NFE class documented under F-002.
findings.rationale: Same class as F-002 on a read route; recorded separately because the route and parameter differ and it was independently reproduced this run.
findings.status: open — observed confirmed; robustness fix deferred to product owners

F-009 (observed; intended 4xx inferred from app conventions)
note: Run 02 adjudications (orchestrator): F-001 and F-002 — inherited suspected defects — are REPRODUCED as observed behavior on two independent seats (engineer suite + verifier real-HTTP probes); reproduction establishes observation, not intent. F-001's intended policy remains unresolved (approve-path policy is not automatically bulkClose policy); its unmet intended requirement is recorded in the finding, and tests assert observed behavior only, labelled characterization. F-002/F-009 confirmed-as-observed robustness defects with intended 4xx handling inferred from the app's own conventions. New run-02 candidates F-005..F-008 all reproduced at HTTP level by the verifier: F-005 dead link, F-006 edit never persists project_id (intent unresolved), F-007 fake-success edit, F-008 control-chars break strict JSON. F-001/F-006 remain suspected-with-unresolved-intent rather than confirmed, because a product decision could legitimately define their intended behavior. No app fixes (frozen). No infrastructure failures on any seat this run.
adjudicationRule: observed-vs-intended: a reproduced behavior is fact; a requirement is only what a source or document states; inferred expectations are recorded as unmet intended requirements, never asserted as passing tests
